findings.summary: The bounded alias row sets `limit: { ...base.limit, context }`. For a Claude model whose base row has no `maxOutputTokens` (Opus, or any Claude model no route names), the alias gets a `limit` with `context` and no `output`.
findings.failureScenario: A route or arm moves to `claude-opus-5-5` (or another unnamed Claude model) with `contextLimit: 80000`, which validation accepts. OpenCode's model `limit` normally takes `context` and `output` together. A missing `output` may default to 0 or fail config parsing, so `max_tokens` is clamped to 0 or the session fails to open. The base row has no `limit` at all and does not hit this. The live test only exercises the Haiku `review.angle` row, and `context-limit.test.ts` just asserts that `output` equals the base's (both undefined).

findings.summary: The usage-reading helpers were switched to `carriesUsage`, but sibling checks still match only `m.type === 'assistant'`. This applies to `turnRan`, and `toolParts` and `turnTools` in session.ts also match only assistants.
findings.failureScenario: A turn whose only activity is a compaction that spent tokens and then failed has `spentTokens` true but `turnRan` false. The two helpers disagree about whether the turn did work, so the retry or 'unspent' branch can treat a turn that billed a summary call as having done nothing. A re-send then bills again.

findings.summary: The prompt-token bound rests on an unmeasured 25% chars/4 undercount (`ESTIMATE_UNDERCOUNT`), yet the schema and docs present `contextLimit` as keeping every call under the bound.
findings.failureScenario: A Haiku route with `contextLimit: 100000` compacts at an estimated 80k. If tool output is dense JSON or code that tokenizes at about 3 chars per token, the real undercount is 33% or more. A request then reaches roughly 107k real tokens before compaction fires. That is over Haiku's 100k long-prompt threshold, so the whole request bills at 5x, which is the cost the feature exists to prevent. The first call and the summary call are estimated whole, so they have the largest error. Nothing in the host compares the observed per-call prompt tokens against the bound, so a violation goes unnoticed.

findings.summary: Messages from a bounded session name the alias key (`claude-haiku-5-5~ctx80000`). `usageFromOpenCodeMessages` falls back to `modelOf(message)` when `options.model` is absent, and `canonicalModel` does not strip `~ctx<limit>`.
findings.failureScenario: Any caller that omits `options.model` (the function is a public export, and the test uses it that way) records the alias as the usage model. That model is not in the pricing or caller-records tables, so the step is attributed to a model that cannot be priced or aggregated. Only `OpenCodeHost.usage` is safe today, because it always passes `h.model`.

findings.summary: The live test wraps an agent step's `host.wait` in `AbortSignal.timeout(90_000)`. Its run instructions also use `timeout 300`.
findings.failureScenario: `rules/agent-limits.md` says: "No wall-clock ceiling. No `timeoutMs`, `AbortSignal.timeout` ... around an agent run." This is an OpenCode session driven through the host. A slow compaction on a loaded machine fails the test as a timeout instead of waiting for the idle watchdog. It is a loopback test with no LLM, so the rule's exemption may apply, but the line quotes the rule's own forbidden construct.

findings.summary: `checkModels` re-implements the `contextLimit` wire check that `routeSchema` already enforces with a refine ('contextLimit applies to opencode routes only'), so the same rule has two messages in two places.
findings.failureScenario: `applyPatch` re-validates the merged entry through `routeSchema` right after `checkModels`, so the extra check adds nothing for an `opencode` route. For a non-opencode route the first error wins and the schema's message is never seen. A later change to the rule, such as allowing a new wire, has to be made in both places or one of them keeps rejecting.

findings.summary: A route patch that moves a bounded route to a non-Claude model fails admission unless the patch also sets `contextLimit: null`.
findings.failureScenario: An eval arm patches `{model: '<gpt model>'}` on a route whose table entry has a `contextLimit`. The merged entry fails the 'contextLimit needs a Claude model' refine, so the arm is rejected. The error does not say to clear the limit, and arms that compare models across families need an extra null per route. No table route sets `contextLimit` yet, so this surfaces only once one does.

findings.summary: The served-models test filters aliases with the literal `'~ctx'`, which duplicates the alias naming in `contextAlias` (config.ts).
findings.failureScenario: If the alias format changes, or a real model id ever contains `~ctx`, the filter silently stops matching or drops real rows. The test then fails confusingly or passes while hiding a real extra row. Building the expected alias set with `contextAlias` over `CLAUDE_MODELS` and `CONTEXT_LIMITS` would keep a single source.
